title: Podcast EP378: An Overview of the 2026 Wilson Research Group Functional Verification Study with Harry Foster
gist: SemiWiki podcast blurb in which Daniel Nenni and Siemens' Harry Foster review the 2026 Wilson Research Group Functional Verification Study: first-silicon success has fallen to 5%, CPU/GPU/AI-accelerator projects have surged, 97% of designs embed processors, and use of C/C++, SystemC, Python and PSS is rising.

insights.claim: The 2026 Wilson Research Group Functional Verification Study reports that first-silicon success for chip projects has fallen to 5%, after staying relatively stable for many years.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A collapse in first-pass silicon success implies more respins, higher NRE and schedule risk for chip designers, and stronger demand for verification EDA tools.
insights.quote: reported first-silicon success has fallen to 5%, after remaining relatively stable for many years
insights.locator: Daniel discusses the recent 2026 Wilson Research Group

insights.claim: Harry Foster of Siemens Digital Industries Software and Daniel Nenni frame functional verification complexity as changing, with the 2026 study results pointing to implications for future verification work.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Rising verification complexity is a structural tailwind for EDA verification vendors such as Siemens EDA.
insights.locator: Harry and Daniel explore how verification complexity

insights.claim: The 2026 Wilson Research Group study shows a dramatic increase in chip projects developing CPUs, GPUs, and AI accelerators.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The AI-driven surge in compute-chip design starts expands the addressable market for EDA and IP, and links the first-silicon decline to harder designs.
insights.quote: a dramatic increase in projects developing CPUs, GPUs, and AI accelerators
insights.locator: The study also shows a dramatic increase

insights.claim: 97% of chip designs in the 2026 Wilson Research Group study report one or more embedded processors.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Near-universal embedded processors make hardware/software co-verification a default requirement, supporting processor-IP and system-level verification demand.
insights.quote: 97% of designs now report one or more embedded processors

insights.claim: The 2026 Wilson Research Group verification study finds greater use of C/C++, SystemC, Python, and PSS in chip verification flows.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Movement toward software-style and portable-stimulus languages signals where verification tooling spend and vendor differentiation are heading.
insights.quote: greater use of C/C++, SystemC, Python, and PSS
